candidates.title: Draft a referral and document intake queue

ease.reason: A spreadsheet mock can list operator-supplied fictional documents; no attached reference supports referral-specific extraction.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: clinics may value a clearer document queue; this paid vacancy does not establish AI-service buyers.

feasibility.reason: A fictional intake queue is testable in two weeks, but document types, routing rules and live access are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: A repeated draft queue is possible, but a clerk must classify items and enter or route records.

evidence.reason: The fresh notice names incoming referral responses and post/document handling, but gives no fields or frequency.

candidates.reason: The notice supports a concrete document intake chore, but no attached building reference supports this health workflow; five modest ratings average 4.6, below the threshold.

candidates.title: Organize a fictional waitlist queue

ease.reason: A spreadsheet mock can sort fictional waitlist rows, but the notice gives no fields or booking rules.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: clinics may value waitlist administration; the paid role does not prove demand for an AI service.

feasibility.reason: A mock queue can be tested with synthetic rows, while priority, cancellation and contact rules remain unknown.

autonomy.reason: The system could prepare a sorted draft, but staff must decide priority and approve every booking.

evidence.reason: The fresh notice explicitly names waitlists and bookings, but not their constraints, frequency or process.

candidates.reason: The notice names waitlist and booking handling, but supplies no decision rules and no attached reference supports scheduling; five modest ratings average 4.6, below threshold.

candidates.title: Prepare a fictional records and reception checklist

ease.reason: A fictional checklist is possible, but the notice does not define record fields and no attached reference supports this task.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: clinics may value administrative support; the notice establishes a human role, not AI-service demand.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic checklist can be mocked, but the named record and reception work is too broad to test as one output.

autonomy.reason: Any record or reception draft needs staff verification; the notice gives no repeatable rule for safe automation.

evidence.reason: The notice names record writing and reception, but does not specify a bounded subtask, inputs or constraints.

candidates.reason: The notice names records and reception but does not bound a safe output; no relevant implementation reference is attached, and the assessment is below threshold.
